source_title: China ruling party says 'eliminated dangers' after 33 expelled - The Hindu
source_excerpt: Beijing China has eradicated "serious hidden dangers" in its Communist Party and military under President Xi Jinping's leadership, a senior official said on Friday (October 30, 2026), a day after authorities confirmed the expulsion of a record 33 figures. In more than a decade in charge, Mr. Xi has cracked down hard on graft, ensnaring thousands of officials and purging dozens of members of the powerful Central Committee and a string of top military brass. China expels generals accused of graft from Communist Party: state media China expels generals accused of graft from Communist Party: state media One of them, Zhang Youxia, held the position of the more senior of two vice chairmen on the Central Military Commission (CMC), making him China's highest-ranked general China expels generals accused of graft from Communist Party: state media storyline 1 As a four-day plenum of the Central Committee wrapped up on Thursday (October 29, 2026), state media confirmed 33 more dignitaries had been ejected, including former Politburo member Zhang Youxia, once China's highest-ranking general. The plenum adopted a decision on "advancing full and rigorous governance of the party", which includes reducing corruption among cadres, state news agency Xinhua said. Proponents say China's corruption purge promotes clean governance, but analysts have said the moves were aimed at paving the way for Mr. Xi to extend his rule at a Party Congress due in the second half of 2027. The Central Committee, "with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core", has "eliminated serious hidden dangers within the Party, the State and the military," Zhang Fuhai, deputy secretary of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI), said on Friday (October 30, 2026). China detains top mapping scientist Zhou Chenghu in anti-corruption probe China detains top mapping scientist Zhou Chenghu in anti-corruption probe Zhou Chenghu, one of China’s leading map-making scientists, is under investigation for suspected serious violations of duty as part of the country’s ongoing anti-corruption campaign China detains top mapping scientist Zhou Chenghu in anti-corruption probe storyline 1 The Party, he told reporters at a news briefing, had been guided by the sense of mission that "we would rather offend thousands than let down 1.4 billion people", referring to China's population. China had previously removed Zhang Youxia, then the highest-ranking general, from his position following a months-long graft investigation, with his expulsion from the party confirmed on Thursday (October 29, 2026). Ma Xingrui, a former top Xinjiang official whose ouster was also confirmed, had previously been removed from all his posts over corruption allegations, including nepotism, bribery and paying for sex. The CCDI's Zhang Fuhai said on Friday (October 30, 2026) that discipline inspection and supervisory organs in the country have punished 7.9 million people since 2012. Efforts to weed out corruption will be "deepened", he vowed, especially in sectors "characterised by the concentration of power, large amounts of funds and rich resource". China’s Communist Party elite hold key talks on governance China’s Communist Party elite hold key talks on governance Few details from the closed-door gathering, held under tight security, will be made known until it concludes on October 29, 2026, but the timing of the meeting is crucial China’s Communist Party elite hold key talks on governance storyline 1 "We will prioritise the investigation of issues where political and economic problems are intertwined, collusion between government and business, and the infiltration of capital into the political sphere," he said. "We will thoroughly investigate new forms of corruption and hidden corruption, and routinely address misconduct and corruption affecting the public at the grassroots level," he added. This week's meeting also saw Zhang Shengmin, who has spearheaded the anti-graft drive within the military and who serves as Mr. Xi's number two in the Central Military Commission (CMC), promoted to the Politburo, the top decision-making body.
